content:
Apple has filed for a temporary restraining order in its ongoing trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI. Apple argues it would suffer "irreparable harm" from stolen trade secrets without a TRO.

In its filing, Apple notes it wrote to OpenAI after filing its initial suit last month, expressing its intent to "move for preliminary injunctive relief." However, Apple said it would forgo such a motion if OpenAI agreed to the following five requests:

  • Stop accessing or using Apple's confidential information
  • Stop any ongoing use or disclosure
  • Preserve all evidence
  • Allow forensic inspection of devices, cloud storage, email, Slack, Teams, and other repositories
  • Search OpenAI's systems for any Apple confidential information

Apple says OpenAI agreed to the first three requests but the two parties could not reach an agreement on the final two.

As a result, Apple is asking the court for a temporary restraining order that would immediately bar OpenAI from using or accessing any Apple trade secrets, preserve all evidence, allow Apple to conduct forensic inspections of OpenAI's devices and accounts, and return any Apple confidential information still in OpenAI's possession.

Apple states:

Apple has also filed a separate motion asking the court to expedite discovery, including the early production of documents and early depositions of OpenAI's key employees and management.

Apple's filing comes as OpenAI published its most detailed public response yet to Apple's lawsuit. In a blog post published in the early morning hours, OpenAI said the "careless, aggressive, and unusually personal lawsuit" is "beneath" Apple's reputation as "one of the greatest companies in history."

A hearing on the restraining order is scheduled for October 1, 2026. The full filing can be viewed below.
